summary_en: This phase 2 trial compares fludarabine, cytarabine, idarubicin, and venetoclax with standard cytarabine and daunorubicin in newly diagnosed acute myeloid leukemia. Fludarabine, cytarabine, idarubicin, and daunorubicin are given through a vein (IV), and venetoclax is taken by mouth; the number of cycles and how often doses are given are not stated. The main outcome measured is not stated; the study is a randomized phase II trial.
summary_es: Este ensayo de fase 2 compara fludarabina, citarabina, idarubicina y venetoclax con el tratamiento estándar de citarabina y daunorubicina en leucemia mieloide aguda de diagnóstico reciente. La fludarabina, la citarabina, la idarubicina y la daunorubicina se administran por vena (IV), y el venetoclax se toma por vía oral; el número de ciclos y la frecuencia de las dosis no se indican. El resultado principal que mide el estudio no se indica; se trata de un ensayo aleatorizado de fase II.
who_for: Newly diagnosed, previously untreated acute myeloid leukemia or myelodysplastic syndrome with at least 10% marrow blasts.
Willing to undergo hematopoietic stem cell transplant.
Adequate kidney, liver, and heart function, and able to take medicines by mouth or feeding tube.
not_for: Acute promyelocytic leukemia, or FLT3 ITD or core binding factor mutations.
Another active malignancy within 5 years, except treated early skin cancers, unless investigator decides otherwise.
Known active central nervous system involvement with AML.
Prior BCL-2 inhibitor treatment within 12 months.
NYHA class III or IV heart failure, or ejection fraction below 40%.
